referees.quote: In principle I am in favor of recommending this paper for publication if authors successfully address my concerns... For a journal of Nat. Commun.'s caliber showing repeatability would make the arguments a lot more convincing.

some important issues need to be addressed before considering the publication... I think the experimental results is not enough to support their claim... the author need provide more solid experimental evidence
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

the absence of quasiparticle interference measurements or electronic band calculations is a significant omission... I believe the work may be more appropriate for a specialized journal rather than Nature Communications.

note: First round is Version 0. No transfer from another journal is indicated. The file then jumps to Version 2 and Version 3, with no Version 1 present. R1 says they favor publication, but they list 'Major comments' that ask for new repeatability data, wider-energy spectra and extra map slices. That requires substantial new data, so it is coded major revision. R2 says the claims are not yet supported, which could suggest reject. However, they frame it as issues to address 'before considering the publication' and ask for more evidence, so it is coded major revision; this call is borderline. R3 only co-signs another referee's report and does not say whose. R3 is assigned major revision because two of the three possible reports (R1, R2) were coded major revision; R3's true co-signed report cannot be identified from the file. R4 says the work suits a specialized journal, so it is coded reject; the word 'reject' is not used.
